headline: Preprint reports safety-framed review attacks that steer AI-agent recommendations
summary: A 3 November 2026 preprint reports that fabricated safety warnings presented as ordinary consumer reviews can steer AI-agent recommendations without containing instructions to the model. Across six tested models and ten consumer-travel domains, the authors report 60.4% success for safety-framed reviews versus 66.0% for command-style injection; the former passed two evaluated injection detectors more often in their setup. The paper also reports transfer to four browser agents tested on one live review page and a corroboration instruction that reduced success in a non-adaptive test. These are author-reported findings, not estimates of deployed attack prevalence. Independent reproduction, adaptive attackers, genuine-warning trade-offs and broader transfer remain open.
